comparison: Both strongly support the overall structure determination and novelty claims (C9, C60, C62). OpenEval emphasizes cryo-EM resolution, AlphaFold validation, and structural database searches. Peer reviewers describe the work as 'convincing' with 'high-quality' density and affirm this as 'the first structure of any member of the transmembrane acyl transferase superfamily.'

Both support the TMD architecture findings (C68, C69, C71, C74). OpenEval notes the internal symmetry and TNAT fold naming, with some inference about functional designations. Peer reviewers affirm the authors 'thoroughly describe the architecture of HGSNAT' and 'define the architecture' without raising concerns about these structural observations.

Both support the LD structural characterization (C78-C84, C130, C214-C215). OpenEval emphasizes the β-sandwich architecture, novelty based on structural searches, and acknowledges lower resolution. Peer reviewers accept the LD description as part of 'high-quality' structural work while noting 'density map is of high-quality, except for the luminal domain.'

Both support the acetyl-CoA binding characterization (C115-C117). OpenEval describes the ACOS structure with MOLEonline prediction, cryo-EM density, and LC-MS validation (C163). Peer reviewers explicitly affirm 'the density for the acetyl-CoA ligand is particularly well-defined, as are the contacting residues' and describe it as 'convincing.'

Both support the dimer interface structural characterization (C98-C99, C105-C110). OpenEval emphasizes the C334-C334 disulfide validation through mutagenesis experiments showing C334A becomes monomeric while F593A remains dimeric. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this as part of the overall high-quality structural work without specific critique.

Both address disease mutation mapping (C140-C150) but with different levels of certainty. OpenEval finds the FoldX analysis and limited experimental validation (N258I, R344H) supportive, noting mechanistic explanations are inferences. Peer reviewers acknowledge the mutation mapping but express concern about 'incomplete experimental validation' and lack of functional data, creating uncertainty about mechanistic interpretations.

Both address LD-TMD interface mutations (C155-C158), with OpenEval finding C76F validation supportive but noting limited testing. Peer reviewers group this with broader concerns about incomplete functional validation, requesting activity measurements and cell-based assays to demonstrate the GFP tag doesn't interfere with function.

Both address scaffold domain mutations (C159-C161). OpenEval finds W403C validation consistent with predictions. Peer reviewers express broader uncertainty due to lack of functional activity measurements, with one explicitly stating 'A weakness of the study is the lack of functional validation.'

Both address mechanistic interpretation (C173-C174) but with different assessments. OpenEval finds the interpretation consistent with structural observations and biochemical principles, though acknowledging inference beyond direct observation. Peer reviewers express significant concern, with one stating the catalytic cycle schematic is 'too speculative' with 'no evidence to suggest that this enzyme undergoes isomerization.'

Both address limitations in resolving mechanistic questions (C193-C194). OpenEval views the authors' acknowledgment of limitations as appropriate and honest. Peer reviewers similarly note 'experimental support for the molecular mechanism...is incomplete' and cite the authors' own statement that 'The structure...does not by itself settle the debate about the mechanism.'

Both address the lack of proteolytic processing (C87, C210). OpenEval notes this limits direct insights into the mature form but finds the structural evidence about disulfide bonds valuable. Peer reviewers express concern that 'the enzyme lacks native proteolytic processing, so it is a little unclear whether the structure represents an active enzyme.'

OpenEval finds the LD-TMD interface interactions (C89-C95) well-documented with C76F mutation providing experimental validation. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though this overlaps with broader mutation validation concerns addressed in R6.

OpenEval supports the evolutionary conservation analysis of TMD across kingdoms (C133-C134, C73, C139, C211-C213) with structural and genomic evidence. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval supports the systematic optimization of expression and purification using FSEC (C50-C59), describing it as 'solid biochemical optimization work.' No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval supports the lack of homology findings (C127-C130) and TmAT superfamily classification (C135-C138) based on sequence and structure searches. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval rates LD function speculation (C216-C223) as uncertain, noting reasonable hypotheses lack experimental validation. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though reviewers generally accept the structural characterization of LD.

OpenEval supports the summary of prior biochemical work (C178-C189) as accurate and fair assessment of conflicting literature. Peer reviewers reference this background (C182, C186) in context of mechanistic uncertainty but don't specifically evaluate the literature summary.
OpenEval supports the authors' assessment of concurrent work limitations and proposed future experiments (C195-C200). No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found.

Peer reviewers support the LC-MS confirmation of endogenously bound acetyl-CoA (C163, C191) as biochemical characterization consistent with structural observations. OpenEval addresses C163 within R6 and R10 as validation for structural findings but doesn't separately evaluate C191.
